title: George Dewey Washington and Paul Robeson
summary: Whaley met singer George Dewey Washington at the Lafayette and the Apollo with Leroy Smith, and says he never knew Robeson but saw him once.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: There was a buy -- we haven't gotten into Paul Robeson. What is that guy -- George Washington --
Yep. I met him at the Lafayette Theater.
George Dewey Washington came in there with -- what's the lame guy that played violin.

Leroy Smith. He came here with Leroy Smith, at the Apollo Theater. And he would drink a whole glass of whiskey before he went on stage. Clear his voice, he said. And, oh, he could sing, George Dewey Washington, yeah. Great entertainer.
He was famous even before Robeson sang that, isn't that right?
Right, he was before -- there was another guy, I can't think of his name. Before him.
Not Clarence. Oh, what is his name? He went out to -- he was out in Lake George.
But George Dewey Washington was quite a performer. He always had a cane, too, if I remember correctly.
And there was a dark man, I remember seeing him. And highly respected in the black community as a performer.
Paul Robeson to me was a great -- he's still great. He went to White Russia, Georgia*, and he married a woman over there, I think. Yeah, he married a white woman.
His artisticness. What did you know about him? Did you ever know Paul or talk to him?
No, I never knew him. But the last time I saw Paul Robeson was when he was at 116th Street in the Square, and Duke had the band there. And he happened to come by. That's the last time I saw Paul.
